According to the Aeronautic Association, Captain Roald Amundsen before his departure for the North Pole stated the flight would probably last a fortnight, hence the Association saw no reason to suppose the explorer had met with an accident.
Nevertheless the Association had requested two naval aeroplanes to assist the vessels Hobby and Farm which at the end of a fortnight would begin a search.

label: text
text: San Francisco, May 28. Mr. Arnold Liebes announces that Messrs. H. Liebes and Company, Furriers, have wirelessly instructed their ship Charles Brower, now at St. Lawrence island in the Behring Sea, to proceed to Point Hope and seek traces of the Amundsen party, on the chance that they have landed in Alaska.

label: text
text: Mr. Liebes helped Capt. Amundsen 2 years ago to prepare a landing-ground at Point Barrow to be used if adverse winds blew him across the North Pole.

label: text
text: Mr. Liebes is of the opinion that Amundsen will travel by dog team from Point Barrow to Point Hope, and thence homeward.

label: text
text: Following the expiration of the ultimatum by the Constabulary, Sub-Major Orville M. Johnston attacked the Sultan of Sa Raya, the disaffected Mohammedan leader at Lanao who has been holding the fort for many weeks in spite of a personal visit by Governor General Wood recently urging him to surrender.

label: text
text: Seven Moros were killed and large number escaped.

label: text
text: A field gun a Stokes mortar and two Navy seaplanes aided in the attack. It is believed the Moros rushed out and broke through the Constabulary cordon when the firing began. It is also thought that the Sultan escaped.

label: text
text: There were no casualties among the Constabu'ry.

text: A recrudescence of the recent trouble at the Japanese cotton mills at Tsingtao has been reported to the Japanese Legation, in consequence of which Mr. Yoshizawa, Japanese Minister, made verbal representations in person to the Waichinopu yesterday, drawing attention to the lack of protection of foreign lives and property.

label: text
text: The reports state that the workers at three of the mills struck work, and destroyed some machinery.

label: text
text: The fresh outbreak is attributed to an agitation by the ex-employees who were dismissed as a result of the previous strike.

label: text
text: Some Japanese were injured in a clash between the workmen and the police, who are reported to have been unable to control the situation.

label: text
text: Seven thousand operatives of the T. Aikang and Nagai mills, who are idle through a lock-out, to-day broke into the buildings by smashing the windows.

label: text
text: The workers hope to force the Japanese owners into a resumption of operations, but the management's declare that the lock-out will stand until the workers dissolve their union.
